texts: good. the sand-glass's kind, its position in the Watch and the village's claim on it all land, and the single objection raised in review (a missing 'a sand-glass is a kind of glass' link) was overruled, since a sand-glass is not a kind of glass.

bad: 'measures one watch' comes out as the sand-glass itself lasting one watch — the span is pinned to the object instead of to the interval it marks out — and 'measures' names no dimension for the figure to sit on, so there is no clean form for the instrument reading. Rewrite as 'The sand-glass runs for one watch.' — a stated duration on a running event is a shape the translator handles exactly, and it says the same thing.
good. reads as a definition: a watch is a kind of period, and it is part of the night.

bad: 'for time-keeping' gets attached to notched candles as a standing property of that kind — a claim about all notched candles rather than about the carrying — because two bare plurals ('Keepers … notched candles') collapse the sentence into a bare kind-to-kind relation that has no room for a purpose phrase; the only compliant alternative drops the purpose altogether, losing it. Rewrite as 'Keepers carry a notched candle for time-keeping.' — the singular object makes the carrying a real event, and the purpose then attaches to that event where it belongs.
